papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.authors: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
papers.abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. We propose the Transformer, a novel architecture based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.

summary.executive: Introduces the Transformer model architecture based exclusively on self-attention mechanisms, replacing recurrent networks (RNN/LSTM) and sequential processing with parallelizable self-attention.
summary.methodology: Encoder-decoder structure with Multi-Head Attention, Scaled Dot-Product Attention, and Positional Encodings.
summary.findings: Achieved 28.4 BLEU on English-to-German and 41.8 BLEU on English-to-French translation, outperforming previous state-of-the-art models with significantly lower training time.
summary.limitations: Quadratic computational complexity O(N^2) with sequence length; high memory overhead for long context sequences.
summary.futureScope: Linear attention mechanisms, long-context window extensions, multi-modal integration.

chunks.text: We propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and instead relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output. The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art in translation quality after being trained for only twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.

An attention function can be described as mapping a query and a set of key-value pairs to an output, where the query, keys, values, and output are all vectors. The output is computed as a weighted sum of the values, where the weight assigned to each value is computed by a compatibility function of the query with the corresponding key.

Multi-Head Attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions. With single attention head, averaging inhibits this. MultiHead(Q, K, V) = Concat(head_1, ..., head_h)W^O where head_i = Attention(QW_i^Q, KW_i^K, VW_i^V).

Positional Encoding: Since our model contains no recurrence and no convolution, in order for the model to make use of the order of the sequence, we must inject some information about the relative or absolute position of the tokens in the sequence. We use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.authors: Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandrs Piktus, Fabio Petroni, Vladimir Karpukhin, Naman Goyal, Heinrich Küttler, Mike Lewis, Wen-tau Yih, Tim Rocktäschel, Sebastian Riedel, Douwe Kiela
papers.abstract: Large pre-trained language models have been shown to store factual knowledge in their parameters. However, their ability to access and precisely manipulate knowledge is still limited. We explore Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) models which combine parametric memory with non-parametric memory.

summary.executive: Combines a pre-trained sequence-to-sequence model (BART) with a dense vector index (DPR) to retrieve relevant Wikipedia documents dynamically during text generation.
summary.methodology: Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR) for retriever, BART generator, trained end-to-end using marginal likelihood of target sequences.
summary.findings: Sets new state-of-the-art results on Open-Domain QA (Natural Questions, TriviaQA, WebQuestions) and generates more factual, specific responses with fewer hallucinations.
summary.limitations: Retrieval latency added to generation; retriever quality bounds overall system performance; index update requires re-embedding corpus.
summary.futureScope: Real-time online retriever updates, multi-modal retrieval, adaptive retrieval frequency.

chunks.text: We build RAG models where the parametric memory is a pre-trained seq2seq transformer, and the non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia, accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever (Dense Passage Retriever, DPR).
RAG-Sequence Model uses the same retrieved document to generate the complete sequence. RAG-Token Model can retrieve different documents for each generated token, allowing multi-document synthesis.
On Natural Questions, RAG achieves 44.1% exact match score, outperforming T5-11B which stores knowledge purely in parameters. RAG models produce responses that are more factual and less hallucinated.

papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.authors: Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun
papers.abstract: Deeper neural networks are more difficult to train. We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously. We explicitly reformulate the layers as learning residual functions with reference to the layer inputs.

summary.executive: Solves the degradation problem in extremely deep neural networks using skip connections (residual shortcuts) to optimize networks with 100+ layers.
summary.methodology: Residual blocks F(x) + x, bottleneck layers, batch normalization, identity mapping.
summary.findings: Won 1st place in ILSVRC 2015 classification with ResNet-152 (3.57% top-5 error) and COCO object detection.
summary.limitations: High memory footprint during training; high parameter redundancy in deeper blocks.

chunks.text: Deeper neural networks suffer from degradation: as network depth increases, accuracy gets saturated and then degrades rapidly. We address degradation by introducing a deep residual learning framework.

Instead of hoping each stacked layer directly fits a desired underlying mapping H(x), we explicitly let these layers fit a residual mapping F(x) := H(x) - x. The original mapping is reformulated into F(x) + x.

papers.title: Generative Adversarial Nets
papers.authors: Ian J. Goodfellow, Jean Pouget-Abadie, Mehdi Mirza, Bing Xu, David Warde-Farley, Sherjil Ozair, Aaron Courville, Yoshua Bengio
papers.abstract: We propose a new framework for estimating generative models via an adversarial process, in which we simultaneously train two models: a generative model G that captures the data distribution, and a discriminative model D that estimates the probability that a sample came from the training data rather than G.

summary.executive: Formulates generative modeling as a minimax two-player game between a Generator and a Discriminator.
summary.methodology: Adversarial minimax objective min_G max_D V(D, G), backpropagation on both networks.
summary.findings: Successfully generated sharp image samples on MNIST, TFD, and CIFAR-10 without Markov chains or unrolled graph inferences.
summary.limitations: Training instability, mode collapse, vanishing gradients for generator.

chunks.text: The generative model can be thought of as analogous to a team of counterfeiters, trying to produce fake currency and use it without detection, while the discriminative model is analogous to the police, trying to detect the counterfeit currency.

1. Introduction 
NIRMAN  AI  is  an  AI-based  road  monitoring  and  decision-support  system  designed  to 
identify  road  damage  and  track  how  road  condition  changes  over  time.  The  current 
prototype  uses  road  photographs  uploaded  by  a  user  or  field  engineer.  Computer  Vision 
detects  visible  defects  such  as  cracks  and  potholes,  while  relevant  road  information  can  be 
used to estimate a road health score. 
The  main  additional  feature  is

deterioration  tracking.  The  system  stores  inspection  results 
for the same 50-meter road segment and compares them during later inspections. This helps 
identify whether the segment is deteriorating slowly, moderately, or rapidly. 
The  current  prototype  is  photo-based  so  the  AI  pipeline  can  be  developed  and  tested  with 
open datasets and sample inspections. In future, cameras mounted on government inspection 
vehicles can collect road images automatically while the vehicle travels along the road. 
 
1.1 Problem Statement 
• Road inspection is largely manual and

time-consuming. 
• Cracks and potholes can increase between inspection cycles. 
• A current road-condition score alone does not show how fast a road is deteriorating. 
• NIRMAN AI detects road damage and calculates a health score for a 50-meter segment. 
• Repeated inspection results are compared to calculate the deterioration rate. 
• The system generates a Road Health Card to support maintenance prioritization. 
 
1.2 Objective 
• Detect visible cracks and potholes using Computer Vision. 
• Estimate road condition using damage and relevant road information. 
• Track the same 50-meter road

segment across repeated inspections. 
• Calculate deterioration rate and trend over time. 
• Generate a Road Health Card for inspection and maintenance support. 
• Develop the prototype using open datasets and free resources. 
 
1.3 Technology Stack 
Component Technology Purpose 
Frontend React.js / HTML / CSS Image upload and interface 
Backend Python, FastAPI Application logic and APIs 
Computer Vision YOLO, OpenCV, PyTorch Crack and pothole 
detection 
Machine Learning Scikit-learn / XGBoost Health and risk estimation 
Database PostgreSQL Inspection and history 
storage 
Training Google

Colab / Kaggle Model training 
 

4 
 
2. Project Description 
The  project  works  in  two  main  AI  stages.  First,  a  Computer  Vision  model  analyzes  an 
uploaded  road  image  and  detects  visible  damage  such  as  cracks  and  potholes.  The  system 
extracts damage information such as count, approximate size and severity. 
Second,   damage   information   can   be   combined   with   rainfall,   traffic,   road   age   and 
maintenance  information  to  estimate  current  road  condition.  The  result  is  stored  for  the 
relevant 50-meter road segment. 
During a later

inspection, the new result is compared with the previous result. For example, 
if  health  changes  from  82  to  68  and  then  to  49,  the  system  identifies  a  fast  deterioration 
trend.  Therefore,  NIRMAN  AI  does  not  only  ask  how  healthy  the  road  is  today;  it  also 
tracks how quickly the same segment is getting worse. 
The  final  output  is  a  Road  Health  Card  containing  current  health,  detected  damage,  risk 
level  and  deterioration  trend.  The  prototype  is  a  decision-support  system  and  does  not 
replace qualified engineering inspection. 
 
 
2.1

3. System Architecture 
The system uses a modular architecture consisting of image input, preprocessing, Computer 
Vision, health prediction, historical inspection storage and deterioration analysis.

5. Features Implemented / Planned 
• Road image upload 
• Crack detection 
• Pothole detection 
• Crack and pothole counting 
• Damage size/severity estimation 
•

50-meter road segment analysis 
• Road health score 
• Historical inspection storage 
• Health score comparison 
• Deterioration rate and trend 
• Road Health Card generation 
• Future vehicle-mounted automatic image collection 
• Future government, GIS, satellite, drone and IoT integration 
 
6. Challenges Faced 
• Lighting and camera angle can affect detection. 
• Thin cracks can be difficult to identify. 
• Real-world size measurement from a normal image is challenging. 
• Traffic and rainfall data may not be available for every segment. 
• The same 50-meter segment must be identified

consistently across inspections. 
• Reliable deterioration analysis requires repeated historical observations. 
• AI results require real-world validation before engineering use. 
•  Large-scale  automatic  image  collection  will  require  suitable  cameras  and  processing 
infrastructure. 
 
7. Conclusion 
NIRMAN AI provides an AI-based approach for road damage assessment and deterioration 
monitoring.  Computer  Vision  identifies  cracks  and  potholes  from  road  photographs,  while 
available road information can support current road-condition estimation. 
The  main  additional

feature  is  tracking  the  same  50-meter  road  segment  across  repeated 
inspections.  By  comparing  historical  and  current  health  scores,  the system  estimates 
deterioration rate and highlights segments that are getting worse rapidly. 
The current photo-upload prototype can be developed using open datasets and free resources. 
In  future,  vehicle-mounted  cameras  can  automate  data  collection,  while  government  data, 
GIS,  satellite  imagery,  drones  and  IoT  sensors  can  expand  the  system  into  a  larger 
infrastructure monitoring platform. 
 
8. Future Scope 
•

Automatic road-image collection through government inspection vehicles 
• Satellite and GIS integration 
• Drone-based inspection 
• Authorized NHAI/PWD/government data integration 
• IoT-based infrastructure sensors 
• Long-term deterioration prediction using larger historical datasets 
• Government dashboard for inspection and maintenance prioritization
